import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

def run(inputs: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> dict[str, pd.DataFrame]:
    dim_customer = inputs["dim_customer"].copy()
    stg_customer = inputs["stg_customer"].copy()
    fact_txn = inputs["fact_txn"].copy()
    
    # Ensure datetime columns are properly typed
    dim_customer["eff_start_date"] = pd.to_datetime(dim_customer["eff_start_date"])
    dim_customer["eff_end_date"] = pd.to_datetime(dim_customer["eff_end_date"])
    stg_customer["update_date"] = pd.to_datetime(stg_customer["update_date"])
    fact_txn["txn_date"] = pd.to_datetime(fact_txn["txn_date"])
    
    # STEP 1: SCD Type 2 load of DIM_CUSTOMER
    
    # Determine which staged records create a version
    records_to_create = []
    
    for _, stg_row in stg_customer.iterrows():
        cust_id = stg_row["customer_id"]
        stg_segment = stg_row["segment"]
        update_date = stg_row["update_date"]
        
        # Find current row for this customer
        current_rows = dim_customer[
            (dim_customer["customer_id"] == cust_id) & 
            (dim_customer["is_current"] == 1)
        ]
        
        should_create_version = False
        
        if len(current_rows) == 0:
            # No current row exists
            should_create_version = True
        else:
            # Current row exists; check if segment differs
            current_segment = current_rows.iloc[0]["segment"]
            # None/NaN vs value differs; None vs None does not
            if pd.isna(current_segment) and pd.isna(stg_segment):
                # Both NULL - no version
                should_create_version = False
            elif pd.isna(current_segment) or pd.isna(stg_segment):
                # One NULL, one not - differs
                should_create_version = True
            elif current_segment != stg_segment:
                # Different values
                should_create_version = True
            else:
                # Same value - no version
                should_create_version = False
        
        if should_create_version:
            records_to_create.append((cust_id, stg_segment, update_date))
    
    # Expire current rows that have a new version being created
    cust_ids_creating_version = set(cid for cid, _, _ in records_to_create)
    
    dim_customer.loc[
        (dim_customer["customer_id"].isin(cust_ids_creating_version)) &
        (dim_customer["is_current"] == 1),
        ["eff_end_date", "is_current"]
    ] = dim_customer.loc[
        (dim_customer["customer_id"].isin(cust_ids_creating_version)) &
        (dim_customer["is_current"] == 1)
    ].apply(
        lambda row: pd.Series({
            "eff_end_date": stg_customer[stg_customer["customer_id"] == row["customer_id"]]["update_date"].iloc[0],
            "is_current": 0
        }),
        axis=1
    )
    
    # Assign surrogate keys to new versions
    max_sk = dim_customer["customer_sk"].max() if len(dim_customer) > 0 else 0
    
    # Sort by customer_id for row numbering
    records_to_create_sorted = sorted(records_to_create, key=lambda x: x[0])
    
    new_rows = []
    for row_num, (cust_id, segment, update_date) in enumerate(records_to_create_sorted, start=1):
        new_sk = max_sk + row_num
        new_rows.append({
            "customer_sk": new_sk,
            "customer_id": cust_id,
            "segment": segment,
            "eff_start_date": update_date,
            "eff_end_date": pd.NaT,
            "is_current": 1
        })
    
    if new_rows:
        new_df = pd.DataFrame(new_rows)
        dim_customer = pd.concat([dim_customer, new_df], ignore_index=True)
    
    dim_customer_out = dim_customer.copy()
    
    # STEP 2: Key the facts against the dimension
    
    keyed_facts = []
    
    for _, fact_row in fact_txn.iterrows():
        txn_id = fact_row["txn_id"]
        cust_id = fact_row["customer_id"]
        txn_date = fact_row["txn_date"]
        amount = fact_row["amount"]
        
        # Find version that covers txn_date
        # A version covers txn_date if eff_start_date <= txn_date < eff_end_date
        # (eff_end_date NULL means open, so it covers any date >= eff_start_date)
        
        matching_versions = dim_customer_out[
            (dim_customer_out["customer_id"] == cust_id) &
            (dim_customer_out["eff_start_date"] <= txn_date)
        ]
        
        # Filter by eff_end_date: either NULL (open) or > txn_date
        matching_versions = matching_versions[
            (matching_versions["eff_end_date"].isna()) |
            (matching_versions["eff_end_date"] > txn_date)
        ]
        
        if len(matching_versions) > 0:
            customer_sk = matching_versions.iloc[0]["customer_sk"]
        else:
            customer_sk = -1
        
        keyed_facts.append({
            "txn_id": txn_id,
            "customer_sk": customer_sk,
            "amount": amount
        })
    
    fact_txn_keyed = pd.DataFrame(keyed_facts)
    
    return {
        "dim_customer_out": dim_customer_out,
        "fact_txn_keyed": fact_txn_keyed
    }
